## Walkthrough

The PR changes DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) error handling in the workload controller. Three resource-resolution error branches now propagate errors directly instead of returning a requeue delay. The supporting constant is removed and test expectations updated to validate error assertion.

## Changes

**DRA Error Handling Unification**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|---|---|
|**DRA error path consolidation** <br> `pkg/controller/core/workload_controller.go`|Removed `draRequeueDelay` constant and changed three DRA error paths (resource claim templates, extended resources, counter resources) to return `ctrl.Result{}, err` directly after updating workload admission status, instead of deferring with `RequeueAfter`.|
|**DRA test case updates** <br> `pkg/controller/core/workload_controller_test.go`|Updated two `TestReconcile` DRA cases to expect error messages ("not mapped in DRA configuration", "failed to get claim spec") instead of requeue-after results, aligning test assertions with the new immediate error propagation behavior.|

## Pull request overview

> [!NOTE]
> Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review.

Updates DRA-related reconcile behavior to return errors (instead of delayed requeue) after marking the Workload inadmissible, and aligns unit tests with the new expectations.

**Changes:**
- Removed the fixed `draRequeueDelay` requeue behavior for DRA failures and now returns the encountered error.
- Updated reconcile tests to assert error messages instead of `RequeueAfter` results for DRA error cases.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pkg/controller/core/workload_controller.go | Stops using a fixed requeue delay for DRA errors; returns the error after status update. |
| pkg/controller/core/workload_controller_test.go | Updates test cases to expect errors (and specific messages) rather than delayed requeues. |

- **pkg/controller/core/workload_controller.go:354** by [@Copilot](https://github.com/apps/copilot-pull-request-reviewer) — 2026-06-08T14:42:24Z
```diff
@@ -355,7 +351,7 @@ func (r *WorkloadReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) (c
 			if updateErr != nil {
 				return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to update workload status for DRA error: %w", updateErr)
 			}
-			return ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: draRequeueDelay}, nil
+			return ctrl.Result{}, err
```

  Returning a non-nil `err` from `Reconcile` will cause controller-runtime to requeue with its rate limiter and typically log an error each time. For DRA errors that are effectively terminal until configuration changes (e.g., 'not mapped in DRA configuration'), this can create noisy logs and continuous retries. Consider classifying DRA errors into (a) terminal: return `ctrl.Result{}` and `nil` after setting the inadmissible status, vs (b) transient: return `ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: <delay>}` and `nil` (or a delay + explicit event) so retries are throttled and not treated as a reconcile failure.

- **pkg/controller/core/workload_controller.go:376** by [@Copilot](https://github.com/apps/copilot-pull-request-reviewer) — 2026-06-08T14:42:25Z
```diff
@@ -377,7 +373,7 @@ func (r *WorkloadReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) (c
 				if updateErr != nil {
 					return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to update workload status for DRA extended resources error: %w", updateErr)
 				}
-				return ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: draRequeueDelay}, nil
+				return ctrl.Result{}, err
```

  This pattern (update status, then return the original DRA error) is repeated in multiple branches. If you keep the 'return error' behavior, consider factoring the common logic into a small helper (e.g., update status + decide return) to ensure DRA error handling stays consistent across the legacy/new/counter-resource paths and reduces the chance of future divergence.

- **pkg/controller/core/workload_controller_test.go:711** by [@Copilot](https://github.com/apps/copilot-pull-request-reviewer) — 2026-06-08T14:42:25Z
```diff
@@ -707,8 +707,8 @@ func TestReconcile(t *testing.T) {
 					Message: `spec.podSets[0].template.spec.resourceClaims[0]: Internal error: failed to get claim spec for ResourceClaimTemplate missing-template in podset main: resourceclaimtemplates.resource.k8s.io "missing-template" not found`,
 				}).
 				Obj(),
-			wantResult: reconcile.Result{RequeueAfter: draRequeueDelay},
-			wantEvents: nil,
+			wantErrorMsg: "failed to get claim spec",
+			wantEvents:   nil,
```

  The assertion `wantErrorMsg: \"failed to get claim spec\"` is fairly broad and could pass even if the error originates from a different failure mode that happens to contain the same substring. To make this test more robust against false positives, consider asserting a more specific substring (e.g., include the template name or the not-found detail) or asserting on an error type/class if the test framework supports it.
